changes_since_r42: Frontend: added a fourth front-door tile, 'A problem I need to solve', to both the main Commercial Workbench hero grid and the 'Your Commercial Activity' panel in app/static/index.html. Routes to content_type=problem_solving via free-text classification -- deliberately does not force a case_mode, so VendorEdge's classifier decides from what the user actually typed. No A3/Lean/Six Sigma/methodology terminology exposed in any tile copy.

Frontend: widened both tile grids (.ve-home-actions, .ve-home-start-actions) from 3 to 4 columns for visual consistency; existing narrow-viewport breakpoint already collapses all tile grids to a single column.

Backend fix (app/pipeline/reasoner.py): found and fixed a genuine cross-contamination bug while wiring the new tile -- the three existing case_mode branches (supplier_request/commercial_signal/category_strategy) each unconditionally injected their own reasoning frame into the prompt regardless of content_type, since they were written before problem_solving existed. A problem-solving case reaching reasoner.py with an inferred or accidentally-selected case_mode (the default inference fallback resolves unmatched text to 'supplier_request') would get a misleading 'you are reasoning through a supplier request' frame layered onto the correct problem-solving one. Fixed with a content_type guard on all three branches. Confirmed by direct measurement before the fix (2,171 characters of misleading injected text) and by a full real-HTTP simulation of the new tile's exact user flow after the fix.
capabilities_included: Commercial Intelligence Kernel -- single evidence/truth layer shared by every reasoning profile
Supplier Request, Commercial Signal, Category Strategy reasoning profiles
Dependency-aware category roadmap with real prerequisite chains and decision gates
Unknown -> Investigation conversion for material market/ESG evidence gaps

Complex Problem Solving vertical slice: Problem -> Evidence -> Root Cause -> Countermeasure -> Action -> Outcome, Maersk principle enforced structurally, validated against supplier/commercial, procurement/process, and asset/obsolescence proof cases
Provider-independent LLM client abstraction across all five model-calling files
Safe buyer-facing transport -- diagnostics excluded from the default API response
Four-tile front door (Supplier request / Something I noticed / Category strategy / A problem I need to solve) with preserved free-text classification
known_limitations: market_verification.py's use of Anthropic's server-side web_search tool remains a genuine, undisguised exception to provider independence -- unchanged from R42.

The case_mode inference fallback (used only when no tile/explicit mode is supplied) still resolves unmatched free text to 'supplier_request' as its default label. This is now harmless for problem_solving cases specifically (the new guard suppresses the resulting prompt injection), but the label itself shown in case_mode/case_mode_source may still read 'supplier_request (inferred)' for a problem-solving case with no matching keywords -- cosmetic, not a reasoning-quality issue, not fixed this round as it was outside the scope of what was asked.
No live external market or ESG data source anywhere in this build.
Complex Problem Solving does not cover Gemba, advanced charting, recurrence learning, or proactive monitoring -- unchanged from R42, explicitly out of scope.
supplier_request_answer and commercial_signal_answer do not carry the same explicit 'diagnostics' separation as category_strategy_answer and problem_solving_answer.
The cross-dimension trade-off detector (category strategy roadmap) uses generic capitalized-word matching -- known, previously-recorded precision limitation, unchanged.
No live Claude/Anthropic API access exists anywhere in this build or the environment that produced it. Every test, including all HTTP-path tests, is deterministic and mock-based.
